A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DEL-ToM, with matching methods and original benchmark results. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ToM experiments on Hi-ToM and Kosinski scenarios, including PBM-guided inference, search-budget comparisons and model-scaling results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds GPT-model evaluations, larger-model comparisons, held-out PBM classification results and verifier-size ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use DEL-generated supervision, binary-cross-entropy PBM training, and the same beam-search and vanilla/weighted BoN procedures. v2 corrects the printed loss sign and expands simulator explanations, without establishing a changed training or inference algorithm.

E1.justification: The Hi-ToM stories and Kosinski belief/control scenarios are retained. The new held-out verifier test reuses the existing generated-trace and step-label task. Newly stated one-chapter and unexpected-transfer restrictions clarify coverage rather than establish changed datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares Qwen/Llama models with and without PBM and against majority voting. v2 adds evaluated GPT-family comparators and a broader Hi-ToM comparison including o4-mini, Qwen3-235B-A22B, DeepSeek-V3, OLMo-32B and gpt-4.1-nano (Tables 1–2).

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include GPT-model BoN with N=4, a held-out set of 2,000 traces evaluated by step-level classification accuracy, and controlled comparisons using 3B versus 8B PBMs. The original open-model search budgets and training setup are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds direct verifier benchmarking, a verifier-size ablation connecting PBM quality to downstream accuracy, and a correct/incorrect belief-update case study (Tables 4–5). These substantially extend v1's search-budget, aggregation and model-scaling analyses by examining the central verifier's reliability and failures.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 3's shaded bands without explaining their statistical meaning or reporting run counts and seeds. v2 introduces no new empirical uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests; Appendix B's probabilities are theoretical.

E6.justification: The original Hi-ToM and Kosinski table values are retained, but substantial results are added. For example, v2 reports gpt-4o-mini at 75.0% baseline accuracy and 93.5% with N=4 PBM-guided BoN, and standalone PBM averages of 90.0% for Llama3.1-8B and 86.7% for Llama3.2-3B. Tables 2 and 5 add further comparisons and ablation results.

T1.justification: New Appendix B introduces independence and answer-distribution assumptions, derives idealized PBM success probabilities, and analyzes majority-voting thresholds. v2 also corrects the recursive epistemic-language grammar and cross-entropy sign. The appendix assumes error-free step scoring, rather than modeling the learned verifier's measured errors.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the headline applicability from SLMs to LLMs generally, with explicit claims of competitiveness with closed-source models. The central contributions—DEL supervision, process verification and inference-time scaling without retraining target models—remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations linking verifier size and belief depth to reliability, identifies failures when updating beliefs of absent agents, and argues for API cost efficiency. Appendix B adds vote dilution as an explanation for majority-voting failure. These substantially expand v1's interpretation and limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link, states that process-label generation code is released, and identifies the Hi-ToM generator and RLHF-Reward-Modeling training code. It also clarifies benchmark restrictions. The previously reported training scale, hardware, training time and appendix prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through epistemic-logic foundations, additional ToM research and a single-trace versus multi-trace taxonomy of inference-time scaling. It adds references on reinforcement learning, distillation, voting and verifiers, and explicitly locates DEL-ToM within multi-trace methods. Bibliographic updates to retained works are separate from these substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, method explanations and related work are extensively rewritten. Separate offline/online results are consolidated into a Hi-ToM section, terminology emphasizes BoN and beam search, and the narrative adds a dedicated verifier evaluation section. This is substantial restructuring beyond merely inserting results.

P2.justification: v2 merges the earlier Hi-ToM tables, adds comparison, verifier and pricing tables, revises Figure 2's accessibility diagram and expands captions. The unchanged appendix prompt is reformatted from narrow two-column boxes into three full-width figures. Figures 3–4 retain their underlying results.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–5 directly assess the previously unmeasured verifier, connect its quality to downstream performance and expose a concrete failure; added code documentation also improves transparency. These benefits are partly offset by new theoretical defects: Appendix B assumes perfect verification, specifies an inconsistent conditional wrong-vote distribution and incorrectly claims zero majority-voting success at q^K=1/L. The empirical additions support a limited net improvement.
